packageRules.description: Build, test and packaging tooling. Nothing here reaches a consumer's rule set, so a green gate is the whole review. Majors stay individual so one broken tool cannot hold up the rest.
Workflow actions cannot change lint output at all. Majors stay individual: publish.yml only runs on release, so an actions major can pass every build and still break publishing.
Nuxt pins @nuxt/kit to its own version and depends on vue-router directly, so a playground declaring either on its own resolves a second copy beside the one Nuxt runs.
tailwind-csstree extends the syntax @eslint/css parses and declares it as a peer, so the two only move as a pair.

The root's typescript range stops at the ceiling of typescript-eslint's own peer, and is raised by hand when that peer is. A widened range would admit two compilers while CI exercised only the one the lockfile pins, so renovate only moves the lockfile within the range.
playground-eslint9 pins the lower bound of the eslint peer range, and a TypeScript older than the one the preset declares, deliberately. Bumping it would leave nothing exercising the floor.

The playgrounds pin different TypeScript majors on purpose, so the example suite exercises more than one compiler against a single preset. A major bump would collapse that spread rather than update anything.
